chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskhan from Sulayman ibn Khalid said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Should I perform some of the voluntary prayers before [the Friday prayer] on Friday?' He said, 'Yes, six rak'at.' I said, 'Which is better: should I perform the voluntary prayers before [the Friday prayer] on Friday, or should I pray them after the obligatory prayer?' He said, 'Praying them after the obligatory prayer is better.'

Thus, the meaning of this hadith is that delaying the voluntary prayers until after the sun has passed its zenith is better than performing them before on Friday. This is not the case on other days, because on other days, when the sun has passed its zenith, it is best for a person to pray the dawn prayer (subh) and then the obligatory prayer. It is not so on Friday, because on Friday, when the sun has passed its zenith, beginning with the obligatory prayer is better, as we have previously established. And the Imam (peace be upon him) did not mean that delaying them is better than performing them before the zenith, as some people assumed.
ai.seo_question: When is the best time to pray voluntary prayers on Friday according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq to resolve a specific juristic nuance regarding the precedence of obligatory versus voluntary prayers on Friday. Unlike other days where the dawn prayer precedes the obligatory one, Friday uniquely prioritizes the *Salat al-Jumu'ah* first, making subsequent voluntary prayers superior to those offered before the sun's zenith. This distinction highlights the unique status of Friday in Shia fiqh, emphasizing the centrality of the congregational prayer on this day.
